meeting_header: Date: 2025-05-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam Ortiz (Redwood); Priya Nair, Ethan Park, Sofia Ruiz (Argentum Labs)
summary: Weekly POC checkpoint focused on throughput tuning. Redwood presented adjusted continuous batching profile and proposed new concurrency targets; Argentum validated traffic shape and raised concerns about cold-starts and tail latency. Agreed to a 24h stress test with updated batching, exchange of traces, and a committed-capacity quote for a short Dedicated pilot.
topics: Continuous batching tuning and batch windows
KV cache hit-rate and prefix caching
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood — we'll kick off. quick rollcall?
[00:06] Priya Nair: priya here, sorry running between meetings, head of ML at Argentum.
[00:10] Ethan Park: ethan, infra. we got sophia as well.
[00:13] Sofia Ruiz: hi, sophia, product. good to be here.
[00:20] Liam Ortiz: liam from redwood, i'll handle the tuning bits today.
[02:05] Maya Chen: quick agenda — one: review last week's numbers, two: changes we pushed (continuous batching profile), three: concurrency targets + queue shaping, four: next steps.
[03:10] Priya Nair: sounds good. our main ask is steady p95 under 300ms at our 80rps baseline, and keep cost within the envelope we discussed.
[04:02] Liam Ortiz: right, so overnight we flipped to profile-x for continuous batching — that shortens the batch window to 8ms for small payloads and bumps the aggregation threshold. preliminary numbers: avg token throughput up ~18%, p95 down ~12% for short prompts.
[04:35] Ethan Park: are you seeing more queueing behind the scenes? we noticed spikes in in-flight queue depth around 11am load test.
[05:02] Liam Ortiz: yes we saw transient queue depth increases — that's from the aggressive batching. we tuned back the max batch size and added queue-smoothing config; that reduced spikes but cost rose slightly on the token side.
[06:12] Sofia Ruiz: when you say cost rose slightly, what's the delta?
[06:20] Maya Chen: ballpark it was +6% token compute for that hour, but latency win for p95 was more meaningful. we'll send the token-level breakdown after the call.
[07:00] Priya Nair: okay, for our product team the p95 matters more than a small cost uptick, but if that becomes runway-eating we need options. also curious about cold starts — some sessions had very high tail latency.
[07:30] Liam Ortiz: cold-starts — agree, those were mostly model load events when bursts hit an idle slice. two mitigations: 1) pin a small warm pool (dedicated) or 2) keep a minimal hot-slot via our keep-warm policy. both have cost tradeoffs.
[08:25] Ethan Park: can you quantify the keep-warm cost? and is it possible in the hosted pilot?
[08:34] Maya Chen: yes hosted supports keep-warm. estimate ~0.9x of a micro-reservation — we'll include numbers.
[09:12] Liam Ortiz: also the KV cache hit-rate improved after you pre-warmed prefixes; hit-rate went 58% -> 71% which explains the lower p50 token contrib. one caveat: prefix diversity hurts cache gains.
[10:00] Priya Nair: our prompt templates are quite variable, so maybe we need normalized canonical prefixes. sophia and i can map top 20 templates.
[10:20] Sofia Ruiz: yes we're on it, will send list by monday.
[11:05] Ethan Park: question on concurrency targets — you recommended 120 concurrent inference threads per GPU, is that still safe? we saw CUDA mem pressure in the last run.
[11:30] Liam Ortiz: thanks, yes that was borderline for the 80b variant. we recommend stepping back to 96 concurrency for steady-state and allow short bursts to 128 with backpressure. adjust KV cache allocation by 10% to avoid OOM.
[12:10] Priya Nair: ok so plan: concurrency 96 steady, 128 burst, continuous batching profile-x with 8ms window, keep-warm of 1 slot for critical endpoints.
[12:45] Maya Chen: correct. liam will push config today and we can observe.
[13:30] Liam Ortiz: i'll also enable queue shaping thresholds — that means requests beyond target get queued with a 60ms soft-deadline before being re-routed to fallback smaller model. fallback logic is important so we don't block user requests.
[14:05] Priya Nair: what's the fallback model latency delta? if fallback is much worse we might degrade UX.
[14:18] Liam Ortiz: fallback model is a 7b quantized variant — p95 ~220ms for typical prompts, so often acceptable.
[15:00] Ethan Park: security note — we need network diagram and SOC2 evidence before any Dedicated commit. who can share?
[15:12] Maya Chen: i'll share our SOC2 summary and architecture diagram; liam can add details about private VPC/private plane options.
[16:00] Sofia Ruiz: on instrumentation — we need better tracing. the sample traces you pulled were helpful but not representative; ethan will dump a 1h capture next run.
[16:30] Ethan Park: yes i'll export a capture from our prod-ish env and share to the redwood SE bucket.
[17:45] Liam Ortiz: one more thing: quantization profile we used (int4-opt) helped throughput but increased hallucination in a couple of examples — priya you raised eval regressions last week, any update?
[18:10] Priya Nair: we ran the 200-case eval set; regression rate was 2.3% on factuality after int4-opt vs baseline fp16. it's borderline but we can tune decoding params to mitigate.
[19:05] Maya Chen: ok noted — we'll run a short decode sweep with top-p tweaks and temperature clamp, and share results.
[20:00] Liam Ortiz: plan for the 24h stress: start Monday 2025-06-02 00:00 UTC, continuous batching profile-x enabled, concurrency baseline 96, monitor p95 and queue depth, fallback enabled. Redwood will provide a dashboard with 1m granularity.
[21:30] Priya Nair: good. also please include cost burn estimates per hour so we can compare to our budget model.
[22:00] Maya Chen: will do.
[23:10] Sofia Ruiz: timeline question — when can we get the committed capacity quote if we wanted Dedicated for 3 months?
[23:25] Maya Chen: we can get you a draft by 2025-05-30; depends on region and model footprint.
[24:40] Ethan Park: any blockers we should call out now?
[25:00] Priya Nair: only the SOC2 docs and the representative traces. once those land i think we're good to run the stress.
[30:00] Liam Ortiz: quick micro-note — there may be small transcription glitches in the logs: k v cache sometimes shows as k dash v or kv-cache in telemetry.
[31:10] Maya Chen: ha, yes fireflies naming.
[32:40] Priya Nair: couple of user stories — if fallback triggers more than 0.5% of requests over an hour we consider that too much. can we monitor that and alert?
[33:00] Liam Ortiz: yes we'll set an alert and add a playbook entry.
[40:00] Maya Chen: recap: liam push config, ethan provide traces, priya confirm success criteria, maya share SOC2 and cost breakdown, schedule 24h stress test.
[41:12] Priya Nair: agreed.
[42:00] Sofia Ruiz: thanks all.
[42:20] Maya Chen: thanks team — we'll follow up in the thread. end.
